[
  {
    "i": 0,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": "FASn0.5Pb0.5I3",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 22.5, "unit": "%", "anchor": "FASn 0.5 Pb 0.5 I 3 PSCs utilizing MXene‐NiO x HTLs achieved a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.50% (20.04% certified), among the highest efficiencies reported for FA‐based Sn‐Pb PSCs with NiO x HTLs."},
    "pce_certified": {"value": 20.04, "unit": "%", "anchor": "FASn 0.5 Pb 0.5 I 3 PSCs utilizing MXene‐NiO x HTLs achieved a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.50% (20.04% certified), among the highest efficiencies reported for FA‐based Sn‐Pb PSCs with NiO x HTLs."},
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": {"value": 600, "unit": "h", "anchor": "unencapsulated devices show improved stability, retaining approximately 80% of their initial PCE after 600 h of continuous operation at maximum power point."},
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Adding 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes to NiOx enhances the conductivity of the NiOx layer without increasing the Ni3+ concentration.", "anchor": "The addition of MXenes significantly enhances the conductivity of the NiO x layer without increasing the concentration of Ni 3+ .", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The ─OH and ─O groups on MXenes coordinate with Ni3+ defects, preventing oxidation of Sn2+ at the buried perovskite interface.", "anchor": "The abundant ─OH and ─O functional groups on MXenes form strong coordination bonds with Ni 3⁺ defects, effectively mitigating adverse reactions with organic cations and preventing oxidation of Sn 2+ at the buried perovskite interfaces.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "MXene-induced dipoles improve energy level alignment at the NiOx/perovskite interface.", "anchor": "The dipoles formed by the MXenes improve energy level alignment at the NiO x /perovskite interfaces, enhancing hole extraction efficiency.", "evidence_type": "inference"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 1,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.08, "unit": "%", "anchor": "Consequently, the PEACl‐treated PSCs demonstrate an impressive power conversion efficiency of 26.08%."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "PEACl at the buried interface reduces substrate hydrophobicity and enhances carrier transport via π–π stacking with Me-4PACz.", "anchor": "The incorporation of PEACl molecules not only reduces the substrate's hydrophobicity, enabling uniform growth of perovskite film, but also enhances carrier transport at the interface through π‐π stacking interaction with Me‐4PACz, thereby reducing charge accumulation.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "PEACl reacts with PbI2 at the bottom interface to form a 2D structure that passivates interface defects.", "anchor": "Furthermore, PEACl reacts with PbI 2 at the bottom interface to form a 2D structure that effectively passivated interface defects and suppressed non‐radiative recombination.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "PEACl-treated devices retain 90.80% of initial efficiency after 2500 h of MPP tracking at 55°C under 1-sun illumination without a UV filter.", "anchor": "Notably, these PEACl‐treated PSCs exhibit exceptional stability, retaining 90.80% of their initial efficiency after 2 500 h of continuous operation at the maximum power point under ambient conditions at 55°C, using 1‐sun illumination without a UV filter.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 2,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.18, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The best power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.18% is achieved, which is among the highest values reported for hybrid SAMs‐modified NiO x ‐based IPSCs."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Hybrid SAMs were designed for the NiOx/perovskite interface using the boronic acid molecule MeO-TPABA as a coupling agent with MeO-2PACz.", "anchor": "Here, leveraging an intermolecular coupling strategy, hybrid SAMs (H‐SAMs) is first designed for NiO x /perovskite interface modification, where triphenylamine (TPA)‐based boronic acid molecule (MeO‐TPABA) serves as coupling agent to integrate with MeO‐2PACz.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Intermolecular coupling converts single-point anchoring into multi-point anchoring of a 2D coupled molecular layer, boosting anchoring density and stability.", "anchor": "Notably, this intermolecular coupling strategy converts individual molecules’ single‐point anchoring into multi‐point anchoring of 2D coupled molecular layer, while enhancing the anchoring strength of SAMs’ anchoring groups—thus significantly boosting molecular anchoring density and stability.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "H-SAMs devices show excellent stability under thermal, moisture and illumination stress.", "anchor": "Furthermore, the device based on the H‐SAMs exhibits excellent stability under thermal, moisture and illumination.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 3,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.53, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The resulting devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 25.53% and retain 90.21% of initial performance after 800 h of continuous operation."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "The PFSBZ additive concurrently inhibits ion migration across crystalline lattices, grain boundaries, and interfaces via a multi-scale regulation strategy.", "anchor": "Here we present a multi‐scale regulation strategy using sodium 2,3,4,5,6‐pentafluorobenzoate (PFSBZ) additive to concurrently inhibit ion migration across crystalline lattices, grain boundaries (GBs) and interfaces.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "DFT calculations indicate PFSBZ prevents direct perovskite-fullerene contact and immobilizes iodide species at the perovskite/PCBM interface.", "anchor": "Density functional theory calculations further reveal that PFSBZ prevents direct contact between the perovskite and fullerene ring, effectively immobilizing iodide species at the perovskite/PCBM interface.", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "PFSBZ-modified films show higher ion-migration energy barriers, lower trap density, longer carrier lifetime, and improved band alignment.", "anchor": "As a result, the PFSBZ‐modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced ion‐migration energy barriers, reduced trap density, prolonged carrier lifetime, and improved band alignment.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 4,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 23.27, "unit": "%", "anchor": "Ultra‐thin perovskite photovoltaics fabricated on this platform achieve a champion efficiency of 23.27% and a specific power of 35 W/g, ranking among the highest values reported for ultra‐thin photovoltaics."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Devices were built on a modified bamboo-derived cellulose vitrimer substrate with a permeable interfacial network from self-polymerizing ammonium salts.", "anchor": "Here, we report a modified bamboo‐derived cellulose vitrimer substrate paired with a permeable interfacial network formed from self‐polymerizing ammonium salts.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The devices retain 91% of initial efficiency after 15000 bending cycles at a 1 mm curvature radius.", "anchor": "Notably, the devices maintain 91% of their initial efficiency after 15 000 bending cycles at a 1 mm curvature radius, while the cellulose substrate enables closed‐loop recyclability under mild conditions.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The dynamic multicovalent networks mitigate strain-induced interfacial degradation under large strain.", "anchor": "These dynamic multicovalent networks mitigate strain‐induced interfacial degradation, thereby enabling mechanically robust operation under large strain.", "evidence_type": "inference"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 5,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.05, "unit": "%", "anchor": "As a result, the S‐P‐F‐MBAI passivation process yielded a device with a PCE of 25.05% (23.67% for the flexible device)."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": {"value": 1000, "unit": "h", "anchor": "the S‐P‐F‐MBAI‐passivated device exhibited significantly improved environmental and performance stability, keeping more than 95% and 80% of its original PCE after 1000 h under environmental conditions and MPP tracking conditions with continuous illumination, respectively."},
    "claims": [
      {"text": "A polarity-enhanced quasi-2D surface passivation strategy was developed by introducing fluorine atoms onto the passivation molecules.", "anchor": "Here, we developed a polarity‐enhanced surface passivation strategy by introducing fluorine atoms onto the passivation molecules.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Stronger polarity enhances interlayer interactions, reduces trap densities, and improves charge transfer and band alignment at the interface.", "anchor": "A stronger polarity could enhance interlayer interactions, reduce trap densities, improve interface charge transfer, suppress non‐radiative recombination, and improve energy band alignment at the interface.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "The flexible device achieved a PCE of 23.67%.", "anchor": "As a result, the S‐P‐F‐MBAI passivation process yielded a device with a PCE of 25.05% (23.67% for the flexible device).", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 6,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.24, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The high‐power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.24% is achieved with this strategy, which exhibits outstanding performance among the reported values for ILs‐modified PVSK/PCBM heterojunction in IPSCs."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "An ionic bridge strategy using the ionic liquid HMB was proposed to overcome PVSK/PCBM heterojunction energy loss.", "anchor": "Here, a spatially self‐assembled ionic bridge strategy using an ILs of 1‐hexyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (HMB, composed of [TFSI − ] and [HMIM + ]) is first proposed to overcome this loss.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "HMB spontaneously assembles as [PVSK-TFSI]←[HMIM-PCBM], reinforcing interfacial coupling, passivating defects, and building a strong built-in field.", "anchor": "HMB thus spontaneously assembles as [PVSK‐TFSI − ]←[HMIM + ‐PCBM], reinforcing interfacial electrical coupling, passivating defects, improving PCBM film formation, and building a strong built‐in electric field.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "HMB devices retain 99.56% after 1000 h in N2, 97.19% after 300 h at 65°C, and 84.05% after 934 h under 1-sun MPPT.", "anchor": "Furthermore, HMB devices retain 99.56% for 1000 h (N 2 ), 97.19% for 300 h (65°C), 84.05% for 934 h (1sun @ MPPT) of its initial PCE value, superior than that of the control devices.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 7,
    "architecture": "n-i-p",
    "absorber": "α-FAPbI3",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.32, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The optimized n‐i‐p planar PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.32 %."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Introducing 4-FAPyCl2 into the PbI2 precursor constructs a quasi-2D perovskite coating that encapsulates the grain boundaries of 3D α-FAPbI3.", "anchor": "By introducing 4‐FAPyCl 2 into the PbI 2 precursor solution, a quasi‐2D perovskite coating of the grain boundaries was successfully constructed, achieving effective protection of the 3D α‐FAPbI 3 perovskite.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The strategy increases grain size, eliminates pinholes, and forms a 2D/3D heterojunction that passivates defects and relieves residual stress.", "anchor": "This strategy not only significantly increases the perovskite grain size and eliminates pinholes but also promotes the formation of a 2D/3D heterojunction encapsulation structure at the grain boundaries, effectively passivating defects, suppressing non‐radiative recombination, and relieving residual stress.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "PSCs prepared under natural humid air conditions show less than 3% PCE loss.", "anchor": "Besides, PSCs prepared under natural humid air conditions exhibit a PCE loss < 3 %.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 8,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": null,
    "pce_certified": {"value": 27.1, "unit": "%", "anchor": "This synergistic regulation yields air‐processed inverted PSCs with a certified steady‐state efficiency of 27.10% and long‐term operational stability retaining over 98% of the initial performance after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking."},
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "ABSC selectively induces in situ formation of I3− without FA+ deprotonation and coordinates with undercoordinated Pb2+ to suppress deep traps.", "anchor": "ABSC selectively induces the in situ formation of I 3 − without FA + deprotonation, while its multidentate functional groups strongly coordinate with undercoordinated Pb 2+ to suppress deep traps and enhance crystallinity.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Devices retain over 98% of initial performance after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking.", "anchor": "long‐term operational stability retaining over 98% of the initial performance after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "ABSC is compatible with vacuum flash-evaporation, enabling large-area flexible and bifacial modules exceeding 16% efficiency.", "anchor": "Importantly, ABSC is fully compatible with vacuum flash‐evaporation, enabling scalable fabrication of large‐area flexible and bifacial modules exceeding 16% efficiency.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 9,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.61, "unit": "%", "anchor": "As a result, the optimized PSCs deliver a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.61%, while a large‐area module (100 cm 2 ) maintains an impressive PCE of 21.39%, demonstrating excellent scalability and device uniformity."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": {"value": 100, "unit": "cm2", "anchor": "while a large‐area module (100 cm 2 ) maintains an impressive PCE of 21.39%"},
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "A size-tunable flow-locking network was constructed at the buried interface using rapid drying combined with droplet fragmentation to harness coffee-ring mechanisms.", "anchor": "In this work, we harnessed the mechanisms of coffee‐ring formation and employed rapid drying combined with droplet fragmentation to construct a size‐tunable flow‐locking network at the buried interface.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The flow-locking network confines colloidal particle migration during flowing and drying, suppressing macroscopic coffee rings.", "anchor": "This network effectively confines the disordered migration of perovskite colloidal particles throughout the flowing and drying stages, suppressing the formation of macroscopic coffee rings and mitigating their detrimental impact on device crystallization and performance.", "evidence_type": "inference"},
      {"text": "A 100 cm2 large-area module maintained a PCE of 21.39%.", "anchor": "As a result, the optimized PSCs deliver a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.61%, while a large‐area module (100 cm 2 ) maintains an impressive PCE of 21.39%, demonstrating excellent scalability and device uniformity.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 10,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.35, "unit": "%", "anchor": "As a result, the PSCs based on this layer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.35% with enhanced short‐circuit current ( J SC ) and open circuit voltage ( V OC )."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": {"value": 1392, "unit": "h", "anchor": "Furthermore, the nonencapsulated device exhibits excellent thermal and moisture‐resisted stability, manifesting in 80% initial PCE retention under heat stress of 85°C for 1392 h and 88% initial PCE retention after exposure to air with ∼50% RH for 2040 h."},
    "claims": [
      {"text": "An organic co-crystal layer, rather than a 2D perovskite, was introduced on top of the perovskite film for surface passivation.", "anchor": "To address these issues, we introduce an organic co‐crystal layer rather than 2D perovskites on top of the perovskite film in this work.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The co-crystal layer passivates surface defects via a reinforced hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses non-radiative recombination, and increases electron mobility.", "anchor": "This co‐crystal layer effectively passivates the surface defects through a reinforced hydrogen‐bonding network, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, enhances n‐type semiconductor characteristics, increases electron mobility and facilitates charge carrier transport in the perovskite films.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The nonencapsulated device retains 88% of initial PCE after 2040 h in air at ~50% relative humidity.", "anchor": "88% initial PCE retention after exposure to air with ∼50% RH for 2040 h", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 11,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": "tin-based perovskite",
    "pce_champion": null,
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Two imine-linked donor–acceptor COFs, BCTB-BTD-COF and BCTB-BSD-COF, were used as precursor additives in tin-based perovskite solar cells for the first time.", "anchor": "In this study, we report the first use of two imine‐linked donor–acceptor covalent organic frameworks (COFs) featuring abundant surface binding groups, BCTB‐BTD‐COF and BCTB‐BSD‐COF, as precursor additives for TPSCs.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The COF additives address performance losses caused by rapid Sn2+ oxidation, which induces high defect densities and hampers charge transport.", "anchor": "However, the rapid oxidation of Sn 2 + ions in tin-based perovskites induces high defect densities and hampers charge transport, significantly limiting device performance.", "evidence_type": "inference"}
    ]
  }
]
